name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: In the fading light of the chill winter’s eve, Kapitan Borisyuk’s guts knotted as he surveyed the jagged landscape of charred timberland, barbed wire, and smoldering machines. The Orgoth invaders had relentlessly breached their fortified position, clawing inch after bloody inch through the elaborate trenches and earthworks that the Winter Korps had constructed to hold them back. But the Orgoth could not be stopped—not here, at least. Not with the dwindling force under Borisyuk’s command. Though his estimate of the sacrifice required gnawed at his insides like a ravenous beast, he considered his decision, the only option that didn’t mean certain death for what remained of his entire kompany. Perhaps the Orgoth could be stalled. Borisyuk understood the harsh reality: to buy time for his retreating army, he and those willing to stand by him would need to endure the impending Orgoth onslaught. Their fate, veiled in the shadows of imminent battle, was clear—they would fight not for victory but for the slimmest chance at survival and the hope that their comrades would find better ground to resist the invaders until reinforcements could arrive.

name: Name
body: As he assessed his battle-worn troops, he felt the gravity of their sacrifice. Most of those standing alongside him, their faces etched with weariness and resolve, would not survive the night. Yet their willingness to make the ultimate sacrifice echoed the grim determination of their desperate nation. They would fight to the bitter end for the Motherland and her people. The pride they took in their choice, the duty they felt in their hearts, these were the source of their courage. Aware of the treacherous terrain that awaited his retreating forces, Borisyuk was uneasy. The west was hemmed in by an icy river while the north offered only rocky foothills upon which they would be quickly overtaken by the unrelenting invaders. Their only plausible escape route for his kompany lay through the Shadowweald—a foreboding forest steeped in haunting legends and dark, foreboding spirits. He grappled with the ominous uncertainty. What seemed like their only escape route might lead to a darker fate if the tales of the Shadowweald were true.

name: Name
body: With time fleeting and the Orgoth closing in, Borisyuk, his remaining warjacks, and his beleaguered soldiers stood poised on the precipice of sacrifice, their fate hanging precariously in the balance, torn between the risk of immediate demise and the uncertainty of the shadows awaiting them in the haunted depths of the Shadowweald. Black Tide Season 4, Chapter 2 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "The Last Detail," "Hide & Seek," and "Shallow Graves."

name: Name
body: Orphaned by disease and murderous revolt, raised by beasts in the unforgiving wastes, and consigned to death in the gladiatorial blood pits as a slave, Kishtaar believes she had seen the worst horrors humankind could survive—until she encountered the trenches. Plagued with refuse, crawling with vermin, and rank with the stench of the fallen, the trenches of the Khadorans are a more unhospitable environment than Kishtaar could ever have imagined, and the mute Orgoth warcaster revels in the absolute despair of her prey.

name: Name
body:
As the Invaders continually reinforce their positions along the frontlines, the Defenders know it is only a matter of time before they are overrun. Rather than waiting for a battle they cannot hope to win, the Defenders have made the painful choice to fall back and abandon the territories they have held for months. As the bulk of their forces retreat, a small contingent of Defenders is left behind to slow the enemy advance.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 50-point army.
The Invader builds a 75-point army.

name: Name
body:
The Invader deploys to an area 7" forward of the north table edge.
The Defender deploys to an area 14" forward of the south table edge.
Place six 3" × 5" trench templates as shown on the map. The Defender can then place three additional 3" × 5" trench templates anywhere outside the Invader’s Deployment Zone.
Starting with the Invader, players then take turns each placing three additional non-trench terrain features. You cannot place these terrain features within your opponent’s Deployment Zone or within 4" of another terrain feature.
The Invader cannot place defenses when playing this scenario.
The Invader deploys their models first and takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Lying in Wait – While playing this scenario, all of the Defender’s units and solos gain Ambush and Advance Deployment.
Traps – The first time any Invader model/unit ends its movement or is placed in each trench, make a d6 roll on the following table:
1 - Survivors: The Invaders stumble over a small group of wounded but capable soldiers who flee across the battlefield and rejoin the Defender’s forces. The Defender can immediately return to play d3 Grunts to any one of their units. These Grunts must be placed within 2" of another model in their unit.
2 - Flooded: The trench template is also shallow water for the rest of the game.
3 - Explosion: A blast rips through the inside of the trench. Models currently within the trench template become knocked down and suffer a POW 10 blast damage roll.
4 - Rat Swarm: The trench is infested with a teeming swarm of rabid rats. Living and undead models currently in the trench template suffer Continuous Effect: Corrosion. For the rest of the game, living or undead models entering the trench template suffer Continuous Effect: Corrosion.

name: Name
body:
5 - Sinkholes: The trench is full of hidden pits and sinkholes. For the rest of the game, when a model is knocked down while in the trench template, it suffers d3 damage points.
6 - Fire Trap: A conflagration consumes the trench. Models currently within the trench template suffer Continuous Effect: Fire.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Defender’s second turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each trench template they are securing.
The Defender also scores 1 Victory Point each time one of the Invader’s models/units is destroyed or removed from play.
The Invader also scores 1 Victory Point each time one of their models/units exits the table from the rear edge of the Defender’s Deployment Zone.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If five or more of the Invader’s models/units exit the table from the rear edge of the Defender’s Deployment Zone, the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points. If the Invader has not won after 6 rounds, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Kishtaar, relentless and poised, feels a surge of grim satisfaction as she corners the Winter Korps at the Shadowweald’s edge. Her eyes, gleaming with ruthless determination, betray a mix of triumph and anticipation. There’s a cold calculation in her heart—a culmination of meticulous planning and patient pursuit. She is almost content with the grim knowledge that she’s secured the prey’s inevitable demise. Her confidence is unwavering; she’s a predator reveling in the trap’s closure, knowing that the forest’s lurking horrors will soon seal the fate of those now cornered before her.

name: Name
body:
As the Defenders make their escape, the Invaders dispatch reconnaissance forces to hunt them down. With the Defenders’ own scouts probing the area, it is only a matter of time before the two rival forces meet on the edge of a lonely, ghost-haunted wood.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 50- and 75-point armies.

name: Name
body:
Players roll off to determine who is the first and second player. The first player deploys first, up to 7" forward of the north table edge and takes the first turn. The second player deploys up to 10" forward of the south table edge and takes the second turn.
Divide the table into nine 16" × 16" territories as shown on the map.
The Woods span the area within 10" of the east table edge. The area of the Woods is forest terrain.
Players then alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to five features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of a Deployment Zone, the Woods, or another terrain feature.
Neither player can place defenses in this scenario.

name: Name
body:
The Haunted Wood – When a player ends their turn while one or more of their models is within the area of the Woods, make a d6 roll on the following table:
1 - Nothing happens.
2 - Strangling Roots: Choose one of your models within the area of the Woods to become knocked down.
3 - Strange Mists: During your opponent’s next turn, all models within the area of the Woods gain Stealth.
4 - Winding Paths: All models within the area of the Woods are immediately pushed d3" directly toward the west table edge. Models farthest from the east table edge are moved first.
5 - The Hungry Trees: Choose one of your non-Leader warrior models currently within the area of the Woods to be removed from play.
6 - Nothing happens.

name: Name
body:
A player scores 1 Victory Point the first time one of their models enters each 16" × 16" territory that is not part of their Deployment Zone.
A player scores an additional Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each section of the Woods within a 16" × 16" territory that their models are securing.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If a player ever ends their turn while securing all three sections of the Woods within 16" × 16" territories, that player wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Kishtaar’s eyes spark with a sinister glee as her Khadoran prey ventures into the forest’s embrace. Delight courses through her, for within the ancient Orgoth-laden woods lie artifacts pulsating with dark magic—an advantage she has foreseen. Her lips curve into a cruel smile, relishing the imminent clash amidst these accursed remnants. She anticipates the impending chaos, confident that the lurking, twisted power will turn the battleground into a malevolent ally. In the convergence of her cunning plan and the malefic energy woven within the forest’s depths, Kishtaar finds a macabre thrill, certain that these ancient artifacts will tip the scales in her favor.

name: Name
body:
The Invaders have carefully pushed the Defenders into making the mistake of moving their forces into the haunted wood. It is here that the Invaders long ago worked their blasphemous magics to forever curse the wood. And it is here they hope to destroy the Defenders’ forces once and for all.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
The Invader deploys to an area 7" forward of the north table edge.
The Defender deploys to an area 10" forward of the south table edge.
As shown on the map, place an 8" diameter clearing in the center of the table. The clearing is open terrain and the rest of the table is forest terrain.
Place a 50 mm Great Obelisk in the center of the clearing. Then place six additional Small Obelisks as shown on the map.
Starting with the Defender, players then alternate placing three 5" diameter clearings anywhere on the map. These clearings are open terrain.
Players then alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to three features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of a Deployment Zone, clearing, Obelisk, or another terrain feature.
Neither player can place defenses in this scenario.
The Defender deploys their models first and takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Bone Yard – While playing this scenario, any model with a Body Snatcher special can make a special action to gain one corpse token and any model with a Soul Taker special can make a special action to gain one soul token.
Small Obelisks – The 30 mm Small Obelisks can be targeted like models. Each has DEF 5, ARM 16, and 10 damage points. The Invader’s Leader model can channel spells through the small obelisks.
Great Obelisk – The 50 mm Great Obelisk can be targeted like a model. It has DEF 5, ARM 18, and 50 damage points. Each time a living model or a Small Obelisk is destroyed, place a calamity token on the Great Obelisk.
When a model makes an attack targeting the Great Obelisk, after the attack has been resolved, make a 2d6 roll on the following table and add +1 to the result for each calamity token currently on the Great Obelisk.
2–6 - Nothing happens.
7 - Dark Shadows: For one round, all models completely within the area of the forest gain Stealth.
8 - Hell’s Path: For one round, the attacker’s opponent’s models all gain Pathfinder.

name: Name
body:
9 - Strange Silence: All of the attacker’s upkeep spells immediately expire.
10 - Rotting Earth: In an eruption of old bones and foul muck, the attacking model plunges into the ground and is knocked down.
11-12 - Dead Rise: The attacker’s opponent can immediately return d3 Grunts to any one of their units. These Grunts must be placed within 2" of another model in their unit.
13 - Death’s Hollow: Each model currently within 5" of an Obelisk suffers a POW 12 corrosion damage roll and Continuous Effect: Corrosion.
14+ - Moldering Curse: The attacker’s models suffer a cumulative –1 penalty to their attack and damage rolls this turn.
Hoard Revenant Mission: Players who include the Hoard Revenant in their force can undertake the following covert missions:
Defender: Sanctifier — The Hoard Revenant can make a Sanctifier special action once per game while within 1" of a Small Obelisk. When he does so, the Defender scores 1 Victory Point, the Small Obelisk is removed from the table, and all of the Invader’s upkeep spells within 10" of the Hoard Revenant expire. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: Invader: Tower of Skulls — The Hoard Revenant can make a Tower of Skulls special action once per game while within 1" of a clearing without an Obelisk in it. When he does so, place a Small Obelisk anywhere completely within the clearing and the Invader scores 1 Victory Point. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body:
The Defender scores 1 Victory Point each time a Small Obelisk is destroyed. The Defender scores an additional 1 Victory Point at the end of any turn in which the Great Obelisk was damaged.
The Invader scores 1 Victory Point each time the Defender hits an Obelisk with an attack and does not damage it.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If the Great Obelisk is destroyed, the Defender wins the match and receives 6 War Chest points. If the Defender has not won after 6 rounds, the Invader wins the match and receives 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
